questions.text: When reading comparative passages, the passage recommends constructing a comparative matrix. What common error does this matrix help avoid?

options.label: A
options.text: Attributing a counter‑argument’s evidence to the main author

options.label: B
options.text: Overlooking modal qualifiers in abstract texts

options.label: C
options.text: Confusing statistical significance with practical relevance

options.label: D
options.text: Neglecting to tag funding sources

questions.solution: Correct answer: Attributing a counter‑argument’s evidence to the main author.

questions.text: Which case marked the beginning of the shift in locus standi by recognizing that a letter addressed to a judge could be treated as a writ petition?

options.label: A
options.text: Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979)

options.label: B
options.text: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981)

options.label: C
options.text: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987)

options.label: D
options.text: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India (1984)

questions.solution: Correct answer: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India (1981).

questions.text: Right to privacy was recognized as a fundamental right in:
In a passage, the author opens with a Nobel laureate’s endorsement before presenting statistical data. This rhetorical move primarily serves to:

options.label: A
options.text: Establish the author’s credibility through ethos.

options.label: B
options.text: Appeal to the reader’s emotions through pathos.

options.label: C
options.text: Provide logical reasoning through logos.

options.label: D
options.text: Summarize the main argument of the passage.

questions.solution: Correct answer: Establish the author’s credibility through ethos..

questions.text: The government issues a press release stating that it will provide a 20 % subsidy to manufacturers of solar panels. Relying on this announcement, a company invests ₹5 crore in a new production line. Before any formal notification or scheme is published, the government withdraws the announcement. The company claims a legitimate expectation. What factual element is essential for the claim to succeed?

options.label: A
options.text: The announcement must be made in a formal gazette notification.

options.label: B
options.text: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation.

options.label: C
options.text: The government must have acted in bad faith when withdrawing the announcement.

options.label: D
options.text: The subsidy must be a statutory entitlement rather than a discretionary policy.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The company must have suffered a detriment as a result of its reliance on the representation..

questions.text: A direct quote in a passage reads: “We must act now,” said the activist. The author later reports it indirectly as: “He argued that they must act now.” The primary effect of this shift is:

options.label: A
options.text: The modal verb changes from obligation to recommendation.

options.label: B
options.text: The pronoun shift reduces the immediacy of the call.

options.label: C
options.text: The tense shift alters the time reference of the claim.

options.label: D
options.text: The reporting verb ‘argued’ adds skepticism to the claim.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The pronoun shift reduces the immediacy of the call..

questions.text: A passage describes policy supporters as “advocates” and opponents as “detractors.” Supporting data is labeled “robust evidence” while contrary data is called “anecdotal reports.” This framing reveals:

options.label: A
options.text: A neutral presentation of both sides.

options.label: B
options.text: The author’s bias against the opponents.

options.label: C
options.text: A balanced analysis of the policy.

options.label: D
options.text: Objective reporting without slant.

questions.solution: Correct answer: The author’s bias against the opponents..

questions.text: If a table shows overlapping confidence intervals for two groups but the prose claims ‘a clear advantage’, what inference does the passage support?

options.label: A
options.text: The data confirms the author’s claim

options.label: B
options.text: The author’s claim overstates the evidence

options.label: C
options.text: The confidence intervals are irrelevant to the claim

options.label: D
options.text: The prose correctly interprets statistical significance

questions.solution: Correct answer: The author’s claim overstates the evidence.

questions.text: In a passage where the author writes, "Some argue that the policy will increase inflation; however, this view overlooks the stabilizing effect of monetary controls," what is the function of the clause beginning with "Some argue that"?

options.label: A
options.text: It presents the author's main claim.

options.label: B
options.text: It introduces a counterargument that the author refutes.

options.label: C
options.text: It provides evidence for the author's premise.

options.label: D
options.text: It signals the author's conclusion.

questions.solution: Correct answer: It introduces a counterargument that the author refutes..

questions.text: In which case did the Supreme Court refuse to apply the doctrine of severability because the invalid provision formed the "heart" of the legislation, and striking it down would defeat the legislative design?

options.label: A
options.text: K. K. Verma v. Union of India (1972)

options.label: B
options.text: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980)

options.label: C
options.text: State of Bombay v. F. N. Balsara (1951)

options.label: D
options.text: Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1955)

questions.solution: Correct answer: Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980).

questions.text: In Keshav Singh v. Speaker, Legislative Assembly (1965), the Supreme Court established which principle regarding legislative privileges?

options.label: A
options.text: The House is the sole and final judge of its own privileges

options.label: B
options.text: Judicial review extends to examining whether a claimed privilege is consistent with the Constitution

options.label: C
options.text: Legislative privileges are absolute and cannot be questioned in any court

options.label: D
options.text: Privileges under Article 105 are subject to the President's prior approval

questions.solution: Correct answer: Judicial review extends to examining whether a claimed privilege is consistent with the Constitution.

questions.text: A pre‑Constitution statute regulating motor vehicle permits was inconsistent with Article 19(1)(g) when the Constitution came into force. In 1960, a constitutional amendment removed the inconsistency. The statute became enforceable again without fresh legislation. Which doctrine explains this revival?

options.label: A
options.text: Doctrine of Eclipse

options.label: B
options.text: Doctrine of Severability

options.label: C
options.text: Doctrine of Pith and Substance

options.label: D
options.text: Doctrine of Basic Structure

questions.text: What is the typical host arrangement for UN International Days?

options.label: A
options.text: A single permanent host country

options.label: B
options.text: Host rotates annually among member states

options.label: C
options.text: Host is always the UN headquarters in New York

options.label: D
options.text: Host is selected by the Secretary‑General for a five‑year term

questions.solution: Correct answer: Host rotates annually among member states.
